options.name: Wealthfront

options.name: Betterment
options.summary: 0.25% (reported flat $4-5/month at small balances), TLH at all balances

options.name: Schwab Intelligent Portfolios
options.summary: No advisory fee but cash drag; TLH only at $50,000

options.name: Vanguard Digital Advisor
options.summary: Low fee, $100 minimum; TLH availability disputed

scores.rationale: Flat 0.25%, no small-balance flat fee reported
Daily TLH (thin sourcing); direct indexing threshold disputed
0.25% but a flat ~$5/month at low balances may apply
No advisory fee but substantial cash drag

recommendation.headline: Wealthfront is the best fit for fees and tax features at $5,000
recommendation.summary: Flat 0.25% fee, $500 minimum and tax-loss harvesting; Betterment is a close second.

reasons.text: Wealthfront core charges 0.25% with a $500 minimum
Betterment may charge a flat ~$5/month at low balances

tradeoffs.text: Daily TLH claim rests on one weak source

alternatives.when: You want goal-based tools or a lower minimum; check the small-balance fee
You are already a Schwab customer and do not need TLH
You want very low fees, in an IRA; verify TLH

caveats: Source conflicts on direct indexing minimum and Schwab cash range
nextSteps: Check current fee schedules on each provider site

contradictions.assessment: Source 6 cites Form ADV and source 1 says much lower minimums, but source 6 is dated 2023 metadata; unresolved
Both agree cash drag is real; range unresolved
NerdWallet (source 1, higher reliability) lists it as offering TLH; source 2 says no

uncertainties.text: Daily TLH at Wealthfront rests on one low-reliability source
Wealthfront fee not in the NerdWallet excerpt; fee comes from non-expert sources
